tasks.spec:
You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, push or touch .git. Do NOT run a formatter on YAML or markdown. You own only: storygame/runtime/knowledge.py; storygame/runtime/reveal_eligibility.py (new); files under tests/ (new tests/test_reveal_eligibility.py and tests/test_sibling_reachability.py; update an existing test only if a message string it pins changed, and list it in notes.md); scripts/ringer/affordance/sibling_reachability.py (new). Edit nothing else: not storygame/runtime/engine.py, not data/stories/*, not storygame/story_package/*. Keep storygame/runtime story-agnostic: no scene id, fact id or story name in runtime code.

BACKGROUND. In storygame/runtime/knowledge.py, `KnowledgeProjector._candidates()` decides which unearned reveals the narrator may award this turn. A reveal is dropped if: it is already established, or not visible to the audience, or its source storylet already fired (`item.source.storylet_id in state.fired_event_ids`), or a `requires` predicate fails (`predicate_matches(predicate, state.facts)`), or it is not a storylet_realization whose storylet is in `state.active_event_ids`. Those reasons are invisible: a spent sibling just vanishes. That hid a real dead end (scene 3A: entering the medical level spent storylet SL-3A-B, so its sibling reveal 'read the experiment records' could never be earned again, and every attempt logged 'This turn has no candidates'). Realizations inside one storylet are alternatives; an action that must stay available independently belongs in its own storylet.

TASK 1: one derived eligibility explanation, behaviour-preserving.
(a) New module storygame/runtime/reveal_eligibility.py with a pure function `explain_reveal(state, audience_id, item) -> RevealEligibility` (frozen dataclass: `eligible: bool`, `reason: str` from a small closed set of constants: ELIGIBLE, ALREADY_ESTABLISHED, NOT_VISIBLE, STORYLET_SPENT, PREREQUISITE_MISSING, SOURCE_INACTIVE, plus `detail: str` e.g. the failing predicate's fact id). Check the reasons in the same order `_candidates` does today so the first failing rule is the reported reason. No mutable state, no new state on RuntimeState; derive everything from the package and the existing runtime state.
(b) Change `_candidates()` to use `explain_reveal` for eligibility. Ordering, the max_candidates cut and the returned RevealCandidate objects must be byte-identical to today for every state. Prove it: in tests/test_reveal_eligibility.py keep a reference copy of the OLD eligibility logic in the test and compare it with the new one over every knowledge item of the real package (data/stories/continuity-initiative, loaded with `load_story_package`, see tests/test_3c_cue_chain.py for how to load it and build a RuntimeState/RuntimeEngine) in at least these states: scene entry for every scene; after each storylet in that scene fires, one at a time; with facts toggled. Also a hermetic synthetic-package test (build a small package in the test the way other tests do; search tests/ for a synthetic or minimal package helper and reuse it) covering every reason value.
(c) Do NOT change `RuntimeEngine._cue_reveal_available` in engine.py (you do not own it). It currently checks only `requires`, not whether the source storylet is spent. In notes.md say whether that is a disagreement with explain_reveal and show one real example if the scripts below find one.

TASK 2: state-aware sibling reachability check (offline, no model calls).
Write scripts/ringer/affordance/sibling_reachability.py with `uv`-free plain Python (run as `PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv python scripts/ringer/affordance/sibling_reachability.py [package_dir]`, default data/stories/continuity-initiative; also importable). For every storylet that has two or more reveals (knowledge items whose source.storylet_id is that storylet): put the engine in a state where the storylet is active, fire each reveal in turn (apply its `establishes` and mark the storylet fired the way the runtime does; find how in storygame/runtime and tests), and for each OTHER reveal of the same storylet print one row: storylet, fired reveal, now-ineligible sibling, `explain_reveal` reason, and whether the sibling's `establishes` facts are all still obtainable from some other still-eligible reveal or from an unfired storylet in that scene (print 'facts still obtainable: yes/no', and the missing fact ids). Do not claim any row is a defect: some siblings are intended alternatives. The script only reports. Exit 0 always (it is a report). Add tests/test_sibling_reachability.py with a hermetic synthetic package of two storylets: (i) one storylet with two sibling reveals that establish different facts, where firing one makes the other 'storylet spent' and its unique fact unobtainable: the report must flag it; (ii) a genuine alternative whose two reveals establish the same fact: the report must show 'facts still obtainable: yes'; (iii) the same two actions split into two separate storylets: neither is spent by the other. Import the script's report function in the tests.
In notes.md include the script's full output for the real package, and list separately the rows where 'facts still obtainable: no' (the likely dead ends), so the author can review them. Expect SL-3A-B on the pre-fix package to appear; to show it, run the script also against the HEAD~0 package from `git show HEAD:data/stories/continuity-initiative/...` is NOT needed: the current HEAD already contains the fix for 3A (SL-3A-E), so just report what the script finds.

HOW TO RUN TESTS. In this sandbox `uv run` cannot write its cache or download. Use the main checkout's environment but make Python import THIS worktree's code: `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider`. First run `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c \"import storygame,sys;print(storygame.__file__)\"` and confirm the path is inside your working directory; if not, stop and say so in notes.md. Same interpreter for ruff: `/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix . && /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff format .` (ruff must not touch YAML or markdown; the repo is kept fully ruff-formatted). Run the full suite once at the end; it is slow when cores are shared. Do not pin collection counts.

OUTPUT. Write notes.md at the worktree root: files changed, final test result (counts), the reachability script output and the 'obtainable: no' rows, the cue disagreement finding, anything you could not satisfy. Do not claim the suite passes unless you ran it and saw it pass.
